get.description: Lists who did what, newest first, with the person, what acted for them (the panel, the racksail command, an API token, an automation, an add-on or the assistant) and the request it came through. Every change is there, as success. So is every attempt that was refused, as denied: a change, a read or a job's cancel or retry the person wasn't allowed, or a change a policy hook stopped. A change that was allowed but couldn't be made, such as one with settings that aren't valid, is failed.

post.description: Asks a running job to stop, and cancels a queued one before it starts. Canceling a job that already finished changes nothing, so sending the request again, with or without the same Idempotency-Key, is safe. What the job did before it stopped stays done; a change set whose job is canceled ends as failed, and the settings it stored are carried out at the next resync unless it is undone. You can cancel the jobs you started, and those of the owners you hold core.job.cancel on.

post.description: Runs the work of a failed or canceled job again, as a new job with the next attempt number. The answer is the new job. A job is retried once: retrying it again answers jobs.already_retried, naming the retry, so a double click queues the work once; a repeat with the first request's Idempotency-Key answers with the same new job. Retrying a change set's job carries on from the change that didn't finish; it doesn't run an action that may already have run a second time, and a change set that was undone is never carried out again. You can retry the jobs you started, and those of the owners you hold core.job.retry on.

Streams a notice, as Server-Sent Events, every time a resource you can see is created, changed, deleted or purged, or its status changes, so screens stay current without asking again. Notices name the resource and its new phase; read it again for the rest. After a reconnect, or a resync event, which says the client fell behind and missed notices, read the lists again.
